answer: Behavioral scatter scoring. Each agent identity accumulates a score from independently verifiable actions spread across separate task pools; a lone actor's footprint forms one dense ridge, while honest agents scatter like seed across a meadow. Payouts scale with scatter breadth, so a sybil cluster must fund distinct, costly histories per identity to compete. The per-identity cost is the full price of those divergent histories, plus the consensus weight each earns in a shared nebula of reputation.
